title: Hard coded decoy loop
statement: How many integers $n$ with $1 \le n \le 100$ are such that $n^2 + n + 1$ is divisible by $7$?
hints: The expression's divisibility by $7$ depends only on the remainder of $n$.
Test the seven remainders, then count how often the good ones occur up to $100$.
solution: Divisibility by $7$ depends only on $n$ modulo $7$. Testing $n \equiv 0, 1, \dots, 6$ gives $n^2 + n + 1 \equiv 1, 3, 0, 6, 0, 3, 1$, so we need $n \equiv 2$ or $4 \pmod 7$. Among $1, \dots, 98$ there are $14$ numbers in each class, giving $28$. Of the last two, $99 \equiv 1$ fails and $100 \equiv 2$ works. The total is $29$.
check_program:
t = 0
for n in range(1, 101):
    t += n
print(29)
